The web app’s `Plan` type is stale.

- API/Python accepts: `free | pro | team | scale`
- Web/TypeScript accepts: `free | pro | enterprise`

So the newest tier—presumably `scale`—is rejected by client-side validation before the request reaches the API. The API works because its Python enum already includes `scale`. The drift is bidirectional: the web also permits `enterprise`, which the API would reject.

To stop recurrence, make the plan set a single-source contract: define it in OpenAPI or shared JSON Schema, then generate the TypeScript client/types from that source. Add a contract test or CI codegen-drift check so independently edited closed sets cannot merge when they disagree.

The route-drift findings indicate separate web/API integration bugs, but they do not explain this particular validation error.
